title: Head-vs-representation decomposition: is M109's sparse collapse a head-underfit artefact?

device._note: Sparse whitening stays on numpy CPU (M107's arithmetic); frozen-code encoding and all head training run on the GPU (torch device 'cuda' = ROCm/HIP here). HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 is a precondition; device_count must be 1 and gcnArchName gfx1201.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens
parity_guard._note: plan v16 section 4.6.1. Every sealed run re-runs the parity check at startup; a run whose worst relative disagreement exceeds 1e-04 is VOID.

dense.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens
dense._note: A2 trains heads only, on frozen DINOv2 features at r42 (the M109 crossing-budget resolution) and r224 (in-distribution). No trunk gradients run.

sparse._note: M108 arm (a) at 3072, frozen; A2 fits heads on the frozen codes only.

ridge._note: M107's head constant; the closed-form ridge is the converged linear-head optimum and the A2 reference.

head_grid._note: registered before measurement; includes the exact M109 t2 schedule (4 epochs, lr 3e-4) as a reproduction control.

schedule._note: head-only training on frozen codes; identical procedure per family and per cell.

gate.registered_prediction: The converged SGD head on frozen sparse codes approaches the ridge reference (0.2148); the t2 collapse is a schedule artefact, and M109's (t3)/(t4) 'sparse degrades more' verdict stands on representation training, not on the head.
gate.kill_switch: If the best converged SGD head on frozen sparse codes stays below the ridge reference by more than 0.02, the sparse codes are not linearly separable by SGD at a practical budget — an optimisation finding that changes A5's Arm P head choice (ridge-only) and reopens the t2 reading.

numerics._note: float32 frozen codes, float64 normal equations for the ridge reference; torch.manual_seed(109) for head initialisation.
